Unavailable/disabled configuration, a second live Envelope, and provider failure have the documented outcomes. Local stand-ins do not satisfy C42 setup checks.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and technical reviewer; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.

The provider is a local DocuSign protocol stand-in, not DocuSign. It does not satisfy C42 or any live-provider check. It cannot render Sign Here placement in the paper or white /sig/ text; the walkthrough checks only that each Signer carries one Sign Here tab anchored on /sig/.

The stand-in needs DOCUSIGN_BASE_URL and SIGNING_STANDIN on the app and worker, which recreates both containers. The brief forbids that on the shared work2 lab, so the walkthrough used its own lab c3sign from the same commit and images, and destroyed it afterwards. work2 was not touched for this article.
Webhook deliveries were signed by the walkthrough with the Connect secret it saved in the connector; DocuSign Connect itself was not involved (see #888).
In Polling mode both rounds read Signed 2.0 minutes after the provider completion. The guide says an update can take about 15 to 20 minutes; the observation is inside that bound.

The author's limitation that the disabled-connector note was read from code only is now refuted: with a live Envelope and the connector disabled, the note read "Automatic status updates are unavailable while the connector is disabled. …" for both roles, and Send for signature was absent.
Connector setup (Environment, Signing updates, keys, Test connection) belongs to configure-signing and was run only as setup.
